races.name: Betvictor Steventon Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Arabian Light
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's 5yo has solid course-and-distance form and runs on good ground without concern; as the lone confirmed pace-setter she gets an uncontested lead, though her STYLE_FIT tag is irrelevant here as leading is exactly the role she is expected to fill — the question is whether she can sustain it at Listed level off 32 days.|

runners_data.name: Midak
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' 4yo has a modest sim-going record (3/7) and arrives 41 days fresh from soft/standard surfaces — though by nature a front-runner, the overcrowded prominent section means he is unlikely to claim that position and will race further back than suits, a meaningful discount on his chance.|

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners a genuine hold-up filly with a strong sim-going record (8/15), two wins and three places on quick turf — she is ideally suited by a steady pace that sets up a sustained finish in the Newbury straight, and Richard Hannon's yard is in solid form (6/50 T14).|

runners_data.name: Silawi
runners_data.note: A six-year-old with a 154-day layoff is the obvious fitness concern here; on ability he has won at 1m2f on firm and good and his sim-going figures (9/15) are respectable, but a return from that long a break in a Listed race against fresh rivals at Newbury is a significant ask for Hamad Al Jehani's yard (0/8 T14).|

runners_data.name: Al Zanati
runners_data.note: William Buick's booking is an immediate positive for this Appleby 3yo who has been placed four times from five on similar going; a natural prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that position in this shape due to redistribution, which tempers his chance — his best hope is to move fluidly from mid-division and use his good ground form (4/5 sim-going) in the straight.|

runners_data.name: Oceans Four
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's 3yo is the most likely of the prominent types to actually land a forward tracking berth behind Arabian Light given his natural style and absence of redistribution pressure; he carries headgear (p), arrives 30 days fresh, and his form includes Listed-race experience on good ground (4/10f/GOO), making him a key tactical player.|

races.paceDynamic: Arabian Light is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the front, she is set to dictate an uncontested, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over 1m2f at Newbury. Oceans Four is a prominent-style runner who may attempt to track closely, but with Midak and Al Zanati both natural prominent types redistributed into midfield roles due to overcrowding at the head of affairs, the pace picture in the chasing pack becomes compressed rather than pressured. The race will likely flow at a measured, even tempo with Arabian Light controlling fractions, which typically rewards those who can travel smoothly and deliver a sustained finish rather than those relying on a true-run race to close from deep. This shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers with good form on quick ground who can pick up off a genuine but unhurried pace — Persica and Silawi, genuine hold-up types, are best placed to exploit if the tempo is misjudged, but any horse landing a forward berth close to the leader without burning energy will hold a major positional advantage. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: of Midak, Al Zanati, and Oceans Four, only Oceans Four is most likely to actually secure a forward position given Arabian Light's confirmed lead role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Arabian Light Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Arabian Light sets a relaxed, uncontested gallop and the chasing pack fails to mount a coordinated challenge before the straight.
scenarios.body: Arabian Light dictates every yard at a comfortable clip, conserves energy through the turns, and uses her class and fitness (32 days fresh, 6 wins from 23 in T14) to sustain her effort into the Newbury straight; with no rival applying pressure, she is never asked a serious question until it is too late for closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop In Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Arabian Light sets a tempo that, while seemingly modest, proves just fast enough on good-to-firm ground to expose stamina limits in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Persica and Silawi, tracking at the back of a compact field, find the Newbury straight long enough to reel in the leader if she has given too much early; both have strong sim-going records on quick surfaces and carry similar weights at 134lbs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Injection Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Al Zanati or Midak, frustrated by their midfield redistribution, move up sharply to apply pressure to Arabian Light around the turn for home.
scenarios.body: A surge from a redistributed prominent type injects a genuine change of pace into what was a steady race, stretching the field and suiting those with a high cruising speed who can respond immediately; Al Zanati, with a strong record on good ground (4/5 sim-going), would be best placed to capitalise if he manages to assert.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Outsider Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a moderately run contest where even weights, fitness doubts, and wide-open form produce an unexpected result.
scenarios.body: Silawi, returning after 154 days off and carrying the doubt of a long layoff, would be an unlikely beneficiary only if everything fell perfectly; Midak, facing a surface and company step up in grade, would need a very specific collapse of the principals.

watchPoints.text: Arabian Light's pace — if Kieran Shoemark allows a very slow early gallop, the race becomes a sprint home that could undermine the hold-up runners Persica and Silawi entirely and effectively guarantee the result from the front.|

Oceans Four with headgear (p) tracking Arabian Light — if he travels powerfully into the straight in second position he becomes a serious danger, particularly if the pace has been comfortable enough to preserve his finishing kick.|

Al Zanati's early position — William Buick will be aware of the crowded prominent section and may attempt to push forward aggressively from the start; if he succeeds in latching onto Arabian Light's quarters, it changes the pace dynamic from uncontested to contested.|

Silawi's fitness after 154 days: watch closely in the parade ring and early in the race — if he travels sweetly through the first half mile he may be sharper than the layoff suggests, but a sluggish early show would confirm he needs the run.|

Going report confirms good-to-firm for this 1m2f race — conditions are fast and consistent across the card, which favours horses with proven quick-ground form; Persica (8/15 sim-going) and Al Zanati (4/5) are most transparently suited.|

races.name: Pertemps Network Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Duraji
runners_data.note: The sole genuine hold-up horse in the field, trained by Richard Hughes and ridden by Finley Marsh; six wins and places on similar going and has the stamina profile for 2m½f, but her natural racing position puts her structurally last into a race where the pace is unlikely to be fast enough to reel back a controlled front-runner.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on the only confirmed pace-setter in this seven-runner field; won over 2m on good ground and is well-suited by an uncontested lead, though the style-fit flag notes he is not naturally at home forcing the pace — Buick's tactical intelligence will be key to how much energy he expends in front.

runners_data.name: Team Player
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with two wins in his recent history at this sort of trip on varying going including soft; tongue-tie fitted and trainer Ewan Whillans has a healthy 21% strike rate over the past fortnight, giving this runner a live each-way profile as a horse likely to sit prominently and grind out a strong finish.

runners_data.name: Ride The Thunder
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's runner represents a stable in sharp form (6 wins from 23 in 14 days) and Tom Marquand takes the ride; has placed twice over 2m+ on good ground and seems at home in this stamina-test environment, though a career form string of 442-36 suggests he finds one or two too good when it matters.

runners_data.name: Shrimp Shady
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's charge has won over 2m2f on good ground and carries strong recent form (1-2-1-1 across her last four starts); her natural prominent style is her best asset here but she has been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are too many prominent-style horses in this field — if she secures her preferred berth close to Bahadur, she becomes a major player.

runners_data.name: Baileys Khelstar
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's prolific performer enters off only a 10-day break but is in outstanding form with four wins and a place in five outings; has won on good ground at this sort of trip and carries a high STYLE_FIT score, meaning the race shape may prevent her from racing as prominently as her form demands — how effectively Rossa Ryan slots her in will matter.

runners_data.name: Almuhit
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's seven-year-old has won over 2m2f and 2m4f on good ground and the form figures suggest he stays all day, but a recent form string of 39-682 is uninspiring; tongue-tie fitted, his natural prominent style is compromised by the congestion ahead of him in this field, and a STYLE_FIT discount applies — he needs things to go very wrong up front to get involved.

races.paceDynamic: Bahadur is the lone confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field over 2m½f on Good to Firm ground at Newbury, and with no genuine rival to press him he is almost certain to control tempo from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop. William Buick aboard adds confidence that the pace will be managed intelligently rather than suicidally, meaning the race will likely be run at an even tempo with a genuine test of stamina in the home straight rather than a sprint finish off a slow early pace. The field behind Bahadur contains three natural prominent racers — Shrimp Shady, Baileys Khelstar, and Almuhit — who have all been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply not enough room for all of them to occupy their preferred prominent berths behind a single leader; the most likely to actually secure a forward pitch are Shrimp Shady, given her proven stamina at this trip, and Baileys Khelstar, who is in excellent recent form and enters off a short break with freshness on her side. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled single-pace front-runner creating a true but unhurried test over this marathon trip on fast ground will favour horses with proven stamina at 2m+ and those able to track from a handy position — hold-up horses are at a structural disadvantage unless the pace quickens late to create a bunching effect.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bahadur controls, stamina test
scenarios.trigger: If Bahadur dictates a steady-to-genuine gallop and the race becomes a sustained stamina examination from 3f out.
scenarios.body: Buick settles Bahadur in front without contest, sets a metronomic pace, and the field strings out as the long Newbury straight exposes those with stamina reserves; horses who stay prominently and see the race out strongly will dominate. This shape rewards confirmed stayers racing up with the pace rather than closers who need a pace injection that will not arrive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent pair grind it out
scenarios.trigger: If two of the redistributed prominent types manage to push forward and sit on Bahadur's quarters, creating a tighter contest from mid-race.
scenarios.body: The early pace lifts slightly as Shrimp Shady or Baileys Khelstar presses into a position close behind the leader, turning the race into a battle of attrition between the prominent group; the winner will be whoever has the better finishing stamina at this trip. True hold-up horses Duraji and Almuhit would need a collapse in front that this scenario does not provide.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If Bahadur sets an uncharacteristically strong pace and the prominent group cracks inside the final two furlongs, leaving a gap for a late-finisher.
scenarios.body: Duraji, the only genuine hold-up horse in the field, would need a clear run from the rear and a fast enough early tempo to create the gap that her style demands; on Good to Firm ground over this distance with a controlled front-runner, that pace injection is unlikely. Her style-fit score on this surface is reasonable but the race shape works against her unless something goes wrong up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield mover claims spoils
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is falsely slow early, bunches the field, and turns the race into a short-run dash that suits a horse switching off in midfield before producing a late turn of foot.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow gallop set by Bahadur is possible but unlikely with Buick in the saddle over 2m½f, as the jockey knows a crawl invites challengers; if it does happen, horses tracking in midfield with a sprint at the end would be advantaged. Ride The Thunder, who has placed at 2m+ on good ground, and Team Player, a course winner, would be best placed to exploit such a tactical meltdown.

watchPoints.text: Shrimp Shady and Baileys Khelstar will both attempt to press forward at the start — watch which of these two naturally prominent types actually secures a position close to Bahadur, as that horse immediately becomes the prime danger to the leader.

Bahadur's early sections will define the entire race; if William Buick allows an unusually slow tempo in the first mile, the field will bunch and the scenario shifts entirely away from a true stamina test, compromising horses whose form is built on grinding finishes.

Almuhit's redistribution to midfield is the most structurally awkward in this field — as a seven-year-old who likes to race forward, being caught in traffic behind a slow-moving group at 2m½f could cost him any chance before the race properly develops.

Duraji's hold-up profile and 32-day absence (returning fresher than most rivals) is worth monitoring from a pace-shape perspective — if the tempo does lift unexpectedly in the middle stages, she is the horse best positioned to pounce, even if current conditions argue against it.

Team Player's tongue-tie and trainer's current 3-from-14 fortnight form is a quiet positive; Greg Fairley is a competent handler of stamina tests and should have this horse positioned where he wants in the early stages given the absence of a rival to fight for the prominent berths.

races.name: Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Binhareer
runners_data.note: William Haggas's four-year-old has won over this course and distance in good ground conditions and arrives in solid form, though his natural forward-tracking style means he may find three rivals ahead of him for early position, forcing him to work harder to land in his preferred spot.|

runners_data.name: Jasour
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse and wears a tongue tie; his recent form at this track on good ground shows just one placing from twelve attempts in similar conditions, which is a significant concern about his ability to land a blow even if the shape suits him.|

runners_data.name: Mitbaahy
runners_data.note: Charles Hills's seven-year-old is a true hold-up specialist by nature and arrives on a 28-day break, having shown his best form when getting a strong gallop to close into; despite being mapped to midfield, he is genuinely racing off the pace and needs more tempo than Symbol Of Honour may provide.|

runners_data.name: Noble Champion
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old comes from a hold-up position and wears a tongue tie; his best effort was a Group-level win over seven furlongs on good ground, and the drop to six furlongs at Newbury is a legitimate query, though his class makes him capable if the pace is strong enough.|

runners_data.name: Soldier's Tree
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners this consistent James Owen five-year-old who has a fine record of placing prominently and stays well within his pattern; his recent form includes multiple places over six furlongs on good ground and he is well-suited to tracking Symbol Of Honour into the straight.|

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Honour
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for Charlie Appleby on this confirmed front-runner, but his form line of 88-583 on good ground is modest; he sets the pace for others to aim at and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that his chance depends on getting away cleanly and stealing enough of a margin to hold on.|

runners_data.name: Song Of The Clyde
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan's three-year-old carries a 5lb weight allowance and has winning form over course and distance on good ground; he is lightly weighted relative to the older horses and his natural prominent style means he is ideally placed to challenge Symbol Of Honour for the lead and potentially outstay him in the straight.|

races.paceDynamic: Symbol Of Honour is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Soldier's Tree and Song Of The Clyde as natural prominent types to push for early position, he is likely to find himself in a comfortable lead without being seriously pressured through the first two furlongs. On Good to Firm ground at Newbury over six furlongs, a controlled, genuine gallop set by Symbol Of Honour will create a race where horses that can race prominently and sustain their effort to the line are significantly advantaged — the straight six at Newbury does not reward dawdling. Binhareer is a genuine prominent racer who will find it harder to secure his natural berth with three confirmed front/prominent types ahead of him, while Mitbaahy, a true hold-up horse, is also displaced rearward on the map despite being shown in midfield. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner setting a fair but not suicidal pace on quick ground — tilts the balance firmly towards horses who can race prominently or make smooth headway from just off the pace, rather than late closers needing a strong end-to-end gallop to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Symbol Honours Leads, Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Symbol Of Honour dictates an uncontested, honest pace and the race is decided in the final two furlongs on the Newbury straight.
scenarios.body: Symbol Of Honour bowls along in front at a sustainable clip, with Soldier's Tree and Song Of The Clyde tracking just behind, and the race develops into a sustained stretch drive where horses closest to the pace have the decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Song Of The Clyde and Soldier's Tree push harder for position early, raising the tempo and turning it into a genuine test of speed and stamina.
scenarios.body: A stronger early pace drawn out by multiple prominent types spreads the field and creates a race that favours those who can sit just off the pressure and quicken cleanly; horses with the class and finishing kick to accelerate in the final furlong benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly strong and the field strings out, allowing genuine hold-up horses to make late ground through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Noble Champion, who has the class and hold-up profile to find late rhythm, would be best placed to exploit tired horses ahead; Jasour also fits this shape but his Newbury record on good ground is a concern.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Early, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses after a modest early gallop and the race degenerates into a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race would compress the field and make it a raw speed contest, theoretically widening chances, but with a confirmed front-runner in Symbol Of Honour this scenario is unlikely to materialise; any beneficiary would be a horse with elite pure speed.

watchPoints.text: Song Of The Clyde could challenge Symbol Of Honour for the lead from the outset — watch whether Rossa Ryan elects to press for the front, which would materially lift the early tempo and reshape the entire race.|

Binhareer needs to overcome a genuine positional problem; if he cannot push forward past Song Of The Clyde and Soldier's Tree in the opening furlong, he will race further back than ideal and his chance may be compromised before the straight.|

Noble Champion's optimal trip is seven furlongs — watch the market move to gauge stable confidence that the six-furlong trip on quick ground will suit a horse who has looked more effective with a longer run in.|

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the card listing Good — fast ground on Newbury's straight course will promote early pace and make late closers like Jasour and Mitbaahy work significantly harder for their ground.|

Symbol Of Honour's front-running role for Appleby and Buick is confirmed, but his form figures on good ground (repeated 8s) suggest he is more of a pace-setter than a genuine Group 3 winner — watch whether he fades in the final furlong and hands the advantage to a prominent chaser.|

races.name: Weatherbys Super Sprint Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: From Me To You
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with modest recent form (7-7-6), no wins or places on similar going, 75 days off — the layoff and poor sim-going record make this a tough starting point in a 26-runner sprint.

runners_data.name: Wait Geordie
runners_data.note: Strong sim-going record (4 runs, 1W 2P on good), won at 5f good, but hold-up style in a race where the prominent profile dominates; Rossa Ryan will need a clean gap through traffic.

runners_data.name: Bint Archange
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for Richard Hughes on a 2W performer at 5f on good ground, prominent style fits this race shape perfectly, recent 27th at this track (a brief blip) sandwiched between two wins — the strongest profile in the race for this scenario.

runners_data.name: Call Me Tomorrow
runners_data.note: Unresolved style (U) with a consistent placed record at 5f on good (0W 2P), Richard Hannon yard in form — an each-way type rather than a likely winner from this position in the field.

runners_data.name: Sky Secret
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on good ground, prominent racer for Clive Cox — 70-day break is the concern, but P J McDonald can place one handily and the form from two runs is sharp for a lightly-raced filly.

runners_data.name: Vollering
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand's mount has a win at 5f and is prominent in style, archie Watson has been quiet lately (0/22 in 14 days) — the going here is faster than her best form but she maps well for this scenario.

runners_data.name: Ballisty
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race, takes on a big field just seven days after his last run, blinkers fitted, 0 wins from 4 but has shown consistent placed form at this trip on good; uncontested lead is his opportunity.

runners_data.name: Bill The Bull
runners_data.note: Prominent type for trainer Adam Kirby, won at 6f on good — has tongue-tie and showed a wide run of forms including a recent 8th; place prospects rather than outright win.

runners_data.name: Final Appeal
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke runner coming off a 73-day break, prominent style, placed at 5f good — fitness after a long absence is the main query but form figures suggest ability if sharp.

runners_data.name: Leucothea
runners_data.note: Style unresolved, best form on soft/standard and has no runs at 5f on genuinely good or firm ground — going and track fit are both questionable here.

runners_data.name: Nascent Star
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only 2 runs (both mid-pack finishes), style unknown — Hugo Palmer yard is in fair form but this is a very open profile in a very strong field.

runners_data.name: Seathegulls
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with 0W 0P from three starts, all at 5f on good or soft — Gary & Josh Moore operation trending upward but this needs a step forward.

runners_data.name: Courage Best
runners_data.note: High OR 120 but recent form shows three successive 7th-9th finishes at 6f on good, flagged as fades in finish — the step back to 5f doesn't obviously help a hold-up type who is losing momentum late.

runners_data.name: Minster Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Eve Johnson Houghton, placed at 6f good on debut — drop to 5f is the question, but ran 9 days ago and jockey Charles Bishop can use him positively.

runners_data.name: Niewiadoma
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on good, but subsequent form has been a disaster (9th, 25th), flagged as fades in finish — the sharp turnaround in form makes this hard to trust despite the sim-going win.

runners_data.name: Rollthedicebaby
runners_data.note: Sean Levey's mount won at 6f soft and placed at 5f good — prominent style fits the race shape but is stepping back in trip again; Richard Hannon in form and this one has only two starts.

runners_data.name: Etienne
runners_data.note: Single run on his record (2nd at 6f good), lightly-raced flag applies — David Egan is a strong booking for Richard Spencer but a 26-runner super sprint on debut experience is a huge ask.

runners_data.name: Angels Lane
runners_data.note: Won sole start at 5f soft, Laura Pearson rides — the soft going on that win is a concern on today's Good to Firm, and Henry Candy's stable has had a quiet 14-day spell; prominent style at least fits.

runners_data.name: Clueisinthetitle
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with a 3rd and a 9th from two starts, both at different trips — Josephine Gordon will need everything to fall right in a large, likely congested field.

runners_data.name: Kodi Bear Light
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke runner with a solid record (1W 2P) at 5f on good, prominent style — Jack Nicholls is a capable jockey for this sort of cavalry charge and the 49-day break is the only query.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: Strong record at 5f (1W 3P in five starts on good, sim-going 5/5), a genuine prominent type who is likely to find herself further back than ideal given the prominent logjam in this field — her true style is best placed up close, but congestion will dictate otherwise.

runners_data.name: Past Passion
runners_data.note: Two places at 5f good from four starts, a natural prominent racer — her redistribution to midfield reflects not a change in intent but the reality that the prominent berths will be taken; form is honest but the positional compromise limits upside.

runners_data.name: Seed Ya Later
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on good, has headgear (h), genuine front-end runner who will struggle to get there with Ballisty and others ahead — pace has been her weapon and she cannot use it freely today, which tempers confidence significantly.

runners_data.name: Zigazig Ah
runners_data.note: Won at 6f good on debut, placed at 6f standard — prominent type for Richard Spencer, step to 5f is untested but Saffie Osborne will look to use speed early; lightly raced with upside.

runners_data.name: Holliesthedollie
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile, 0W 0P from three starts including an 8th and a 7th — Olivia Tubb faces a stiff task in a field of this depth from this position.

runners_data.name: Devon Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning just four days after last run, OR only 44, recent form shows a 3rd at 5f good but also several double-digit finishes — tongue-tie fitted, Rod Millman yard moderately in form but this is at the bottom of the market for good reason.

races.paceDynamic: Ballisty is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 26-runner field and will stride straight to the front from the gates, setting a genuine but uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground over this straight five furlongs at Newbury. With no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, Ballisty shapes to control tempo from a low-pressure position, meaning the pace will be honest but not suicidal — a rhythm that keeps the rail and a clear sightline to the line. Prominent types Bint Archange, Sky Secret, Vollering, and Bill The Bull will track close behind, and they are the profile that benefits most: sitting a length or two off a controlled pace on fast ground over a stiff five furlongs rewards those who race prominently without burning fuel fighting for position. The field holds more front-running or prominent types than can all secure their natural berth — Holi Scarlett, Seed Ya Later, and Past Passion are genuine prominent horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled further back than ideal given the congestion of the early stages, with Bint Archange and Sky Secret best-placed to occupy the prime ground behind Ballisty.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Ballisty dictates an unchallenged, even gallop and the prominent trackers settle cleanly in a two-wide pack behind
scenarios.body: Bint Archange, Vollering, Sky Secret, and Bill The Bull will be able to race within a length of the pace and produce their effort from the two-furlong pole, exactly the pattern this track rewards in 5f sprints on quick ground; horses with the best form figures at this trip on similar ground — particularly Bint Archange (2W at 5f good) and Kodi Bear Light — are squarely in the frame.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Ballisty's uncontested lead translates into a bowled-along gallop that is never truly challenged and the field is slow to respond in the straight
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied early, Ballisty could conserve enough energy to extend and hold on, particularly if the prominent horses jostle and lose momentum in a big field; Ballisty's headgear (b) and sharp recent return (7 days ago) suggest readiness, and the lack of a chasing pack is a genuine risk for the hold-up types to close down.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Weave Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group is tightly bunched and creates enough early pace that the hold-up horses get a genuine gap to fill in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Wait Geordie and Bint Archange (who has both hold-up and prominent gears) could pounce if the prominent wall fractures, and late-running types like Wait Geordie — who won at 5f good and has strong sim-going form — could benefit from a track position further back than expected; this scenario is diluted by the fact that several of the mapped midfield horses are redistributed true-prominent types running out of role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large 26-runner field fans wide at the two-furlong pole and pace collapses into a blanket finish with no clear run for any horse
scenarios.body: Lightly-raced or unexposed runners like Etienne, Angels Lane, and Zigazig Ah could emerge from the pack having avoided early trouble, but this is a low-probability shape because Ballisty's uncontested lead and the organised prominent group reduce the chance of a total pace meltdown; the scenario rewards any runner who secures a clean outside draw and a clear passage late.

watchPoints.text: Ballisty (the lone front-runner) sets the entire race shape — if he jumps cleanly and establishes uncontested lead within the first furlong, prominent trackers Bint Archange and Sky Secret will be the ones to beat.

With 26 runners over 5f, watch for a crowded break in the first two furlongs — Seed Ya Later, Holi Scarlett, and Past Passion are all genuine prominent horses who will be squeezed for position and may lose several lengths at the start.

Courage Best and Niewiadoma are both flagged as faders — despite their high ORs, any horse that needs cover and then fades on fast ground is vulnerable in a flat-out sprint, particularly Niewiadoma whose form collapse after her win is stark.

Final Appeal returns from 73 days off and Sky Secret from 70 days — fitness of both after lengthy breaks could be decisive if their prominent style would otherwise have them right in contention; watch for signs of greenness or a laboured finish.

The going report consistently confirms Good to Firm for this race (not just Good as declared) — runners with form on soft or yielding ground, including Angels Lane (sole win on soft) and Leucothea (best form on soft/standard), face a meaningful surface query.

runners_data.name: All Moonshine
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's mare is the race's natural pace-setter, clocking a win in her last three starts including back-to-back victories at Sandown at this trip, though her sole form on Good ground produced a fifth — the step up in class and likely softer fractions on faster ground make her a pace factor rather than a guaranteed winner; STYLE_FIT flag is minor given she is actually slotted into a lead role here.|

runners_data.name: New Vega
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford's three-year-old returns from a 338-day absence having won at 7f on Good at Goodwood last time — that form reads well for this trip and surface, and Rossa Ryan's booking is eye-catching; the question is fitness after nearly a year off, though a yard with a 6/21 14-day strike rate suggests horses arrive ready.|

runners_data.name: Tavana
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne's filly has struggled recently, posting 8-11-9 finishes in her last three on Good ground at a mile, and the drop back to seven furlongs 14 days ago yielded a mid-field fourth at best; Sean Levey takes the ride but the form figures inspire little confidence for a prominent finish.|

runners_data.name: Brisk Symphony
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's three-year-old has placed in her last two starts at seven furlongs, including a second on Good ground, and Rob Hornby partners her as a natural prominent type who will push forward; the key question is whether she can sustain that position to the line rather than simply handing the front to All Moonshine.|

runners_data.name: Lightning Polka
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly wears a hood and has shown ability at this trip on Good ground with a recent third, but she has also produced a tenth from six similar-going starts and her form is streaky; Kieran Shoemark rides and as a genuine hold-up type she needs either a fast pace to chase or a perfectly-timed run through traffic.|

runners_data.name: Velvet Rhythm
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly owns four wins from nine runs on similar going at seven furlongs and is a standout on form figures — however, she is a natural front-runner or prominent racer and in a field where All Moonshine holds the lead and Brisk Symphony claims the rail berth, she may find herself unable to settle in her preferred spot; Saffie Osborne must work tactically to compensate for the compromised position.|

races.paceDynamic: All Moonshine is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Brisk Symphony as a natural rival for the early lead, she is set to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over seven furlongs. Brisk Symphony will push forward to track or press for the prominent berth, but with just six runners and no one likely to force a genuinely fierce pace, the tempo should be honest rather than scorching. Velvet Rhythm is a natural prominent racer who has been redistributed to a midfield position on the map because All Moonshine and Brisk Symphony will fill the front slots — she may not secure her preferred pitch and that complicates her task. This controlled, single-pacemaker shape on a flat, fast-ground track over seven furlongs classically rewards horses who can settle just off the leader and produce a sustained, clean finish — the prominent-to-midfield profile with a turn of foot suits best, not deep closers who need genuine pressure to be set.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moonshine Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If All Moonshine dictates an unchallenged, measured gallop and the race unfolds in a steady, strung-out fashion from halfway.
scenarios.body: All Moonshine sets fractions she is comfortable with, leaving those close to her with a clean passage and a test of finishing quality rather than stamina; the horse travelling best just off the pace gets first run and the advantage is rarely surrendered on flat, fast ground. New Vega and Brisk Symphony, both equipped to sit within a length or two, are the profiles that cash in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Brisk Symphony Presses, Pace Lifts
scenarios.trigger: If Brisk Symphony contests the lead more aggressively than expected, forcing a genuinely contested gallop in the first three furlongs.
scenarios.body: A pressured front end raises the tempo enough to stretch the field and rewards horses with genuine reserves over the final two furlongs; the race becomes more about who handles the faster early fractions rather than a pure sprint finish. Lightning Polka, who has placed on Good ground at this trip, and New Vega, a winner on Good, are the profiles suited if the pace quickens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and the backmarkers find a gap to run through.
scenarios.body: Tavana and Lightning Polka would need the leaders to fold entirely, which requires a faster-than-expected early gallop to have drained front-runners' reserves; this is a low-probability outcome because All Moonshine has proven she can sustain her effort and the small field gives closers less cover and traffic to navigate. Both are genuine hold-up types but their recent form figures are inconsistent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Velvet Rhythm Recovers Position
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Rhythm overcomes her redistributed disadvantage and gets close enough to the pace to unleash her natural prominent-racer finish.
scenarios.body: Velvet Rhythm has a strong form record on Good ground at seven furlongs, with four wins from nine similar-going runs, but she is not operating in her natural zone in this map and the margin for error is tight; if she does secure a position forward of midfield she becomes dangerous, though the small field makes that recovery harder against horses already drawn into their natural roles. Her chance hinges almost entirely on tactical luck.

watchPoints.text: All Moonshine's sole run on Good ground produced a poor effort — if the Good to Firm strip at Newbury rides genuinely quick, monitor her in the market for any late confidence-draining moves.

Velvet Rhythm's inability to secure her natural prominent pitch in this six-runner field is the single biggest race-shape complication — watch her early stride pattern for signs she is already losing ground to Brisk Symphony off the gates.
New Vega returns from 338 days off and, while the Crisford yard fires horses fresh, watch for any market drift in the final hour that would signal stable reservations about her fitness.

Lightning Polka's hood is noted — first-time or repeated headgear use can produce an unpredictable early jump from the stalls; in a small field over seven furlongs, any positional chaos in the opening two furlongs would directly disturb the controlled shape that suits the pace map.

Brisk Symphony's jockey Rob Hornby will determine whether this race is truly run at an easy All Moonshine-controlled tempo or something more competitive — if she pushes forward aggressively rather than sitting second, the entire pace dynamic shifts toward Scenario B.
